title: The New Normal for Cruise
gist: Promotional page for an 18 Nov 2026 Tourism Economics/Oxford Economics webinar: after strong growth since the 2021 post-Covid restart, new cruise capacity is now slowing and a 'new normal' is reshaping which regions and ports benefit as cruise lines rethink fleet deployment.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics' Tourism Economics says the cruise sector, after strong growth since its 2021 post-Covid restart, is entering a phase of slowing new capacity that makes the industry of 2027 look very different from 2019.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Slowing fleet additions typically support cruise-line pricing and yields while reducing shipyard order momentum.
insights.quote: After strong growth since the 2021 post-Covid restart, and with new capacity now slowing
insights.locator: The cruise sector today looks very different

insights.claim: Tourism Economics expects the cruise 'new normal' to reshape prospects for cruise regions and ports as cruise lines rethink where and how they deploy their fleets.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Port operators and destination economies face redistribution of cruise calls; deployment shifts are a watch item for regional tourism exposure.
